questions.stem: Why is the refractory period important in nerve impulse transmission?

options.text: It allows the myelin sheath to regenerate
It ensures impulses only travel in one direction along the neurone
It increases the speed of impulse transmission
It allows the neurone to produce more neurotransmitters

questions.explanation: The refractory period is a short time after an action potential during which the neurone cannot fire again. This ensures impulses travel in one direction and allows the neurone to recover.
